The Craelius core orientator can operate in steeply inclined or horizontal
boreholes as well as vertical holes, but it does not provide information on the
aperture or infilling of discontinuities, nor does it provide a permanent record
of discontinuities. In addition, the orientation of the core must be determined
relative to the uppermost core segment, and this may prove difficult where
core recovery is poor or where the core contains sub-horizontal joints (Gamon,
1984a).
